newsitem.title: USA: Dow Jones says to stay independent - report.
newsitem.headline: Dow Jones says to stay independent - report.

text.p: Financial information company Dow Jones & Co Inc plans to remain independent despite reports about rivals interested in buying a stake in it, the company's chief executive told a weekly news magazine.

"The board (of directors) and (controlling shareholders) the Bancroft family have made it clear that Dow Jones intends to remain fully independent," Peter Kann told Business Week. "I think we are doing fine on our own."

Local news reports published in the last few months have mentioned apparent interest on the part of General Electric Co, which owns the NBC television network, Reuters Holdings Plc and Bloomberg LP to buy into the company.
Reuters, which competes with Dow Jones in the financial news and information markets, has declined to comment on the reports, describing them as rumours.
Dow Jones has plans to spend $650 million to expand and revitalize its Telerate financial information services unit, whose name was recently changed to Dow Jones Markets.
But Bancroft family members are apparently unhappy with the plans and want the company to improve shareholder value.
Kann, however, denied there was any turmoil at Dow Jones.
"I think we have some business issues that we are addressing," he said. "I think that the future of this company is very bright."
On Thursday, a federal jury awarded a defunct securities firm $223 million for damages in a libel suit against the company.
Dow Jones said the decision would be appealed.
